summary: Created Unity-owned wire schemas/parsers (unity-wire.ts) in packages/unity, re-exported UnityStatus from types.ts, rewrote the Unity web domain-plugin to use per-extension store shapes via parseUnityStatus/parseUnityOpenProjectResult, and updated UnityHost plus EditorPanel.svelte to read projectOpening[unity]/projectServiceErrors[unity].
decisions: Per-extension project-opening state is exposed as projectOpening: Record<string, boolean>; UnityPanel reads store.projectOpening.unity
Per-extension project-service errors are exposed as projectServiceErrors: Record<string, string>; EditorPanel falls back to store.projectServiceErrors.unity
UnityStatus is now owned by the Unity extension (unity-wire.ts) using TypeBox schemas with a local UnityProtocolValidationError; core treats the wire payload as opaque per protocol v26
The UnityStatus type is re-exported from types.ts rather than duplicated, so existing consumers (unity-view.test.ts) keep working

Project-service coexistence/routing tests added in the lifecycle file were extracted into their own test file to avoid pushing websocket-server.lifecycle.test.ts over the 300-line check:loc limit (pre-existing over-limit files were confirmed unchanged at HEAD)
errors: pnpm check failed because websocket-server.lifecycle.test.ts grew to 451 lines (>300). Four other over-limit files (skills-library.css, layout.css, resource-catalog.ts, session-runtime-pool.ts) were verified to be pre-existing at HEAD, not introduced by this work.
An accidental `git stash` captured the user's working tree; it was immediately restored via `git stash pop` with no loss.
